In July 1609 the English ship Sea Venture, carrying settlers to Jamestown in Virginia, was wrecked on the reefs of Bermuda in a storm. All on board reached land.

The castaways, led by Admiral George Somers, lived on the island for ten months and built two small ships, which carried most of them on to Virginia in 1610. They found the struggling colony starving and helped save it.

Their story reached London and is thought to have inspired Shakespeare in The Tempest. England claimed Bermuda, and settlers arrived in 1612 and founded St George's. Bermuda is the oldest British overseas territory.
